title: When incentives backfire
blurb: Set a target, reward a number, and watch people optimise the number instead of the thing you wanted. These are the laws of measures gone wrong.

title: The razors
blurb: A razor is a rule for shaving away the unlikely. When two explanations compete, these are the heuristics that tell you which to reach for first.

title: Biases that skew decisions
blurb: The mind takes shortcuts, and the shortcuts have a shape. Learn the shape and you can catch yourself mid-mistake.

title: Why estimates are always wrong
blurb: Every plan is a forecast, and forecasts fail in patterned ways. These laws explain why the work runs long no matter how carefully you counted.
